messages:
Sam W: Heads-up — BlueHarbor wants to migrate from RivalAPI into Redwood. They ran a quick POC and called out prompt parity failures and response-shape differences. Also asked about pricing deltas and a security questionnaire. Can we assemble answers + a short runbook?
Mia - Sales: Thanks. Do we know which RivalAPI endpoints/features they rely on? streaming, function calling, embeddings?
Sam W: Main ones: streaming chat with partial tokens, function-calling webhooks, and embeddings for search. They also use policy-based rate limits and had expectations about stop-sequence behavior.
Leila - Solutions: Ok — high level: 1) Prompt parity: RivalAPI applies a default stop/trim behavior that we don't by default, so some of their prompts return extra tokens. 2) Function calling: RivalAPI returns richer structured args in some cases; we'll need a mapping layer for field names. 3) Streaming: RivalAPI flushes on sentence boundaries which affects perceived latency. 4) Embeddings: rival uses a different normalization + dimension (they do 1536 floats); need a migration plan for reindexing.
Oliver (Eng): Technically doable. Suggested approach: lightweight compatibility shim that: a) rewrites request parameters (stop sequences, temperature, max_tokens) to our equivalents, b) post-processes response JSON to match RivalAPI shapes, c) optionally runs a delta-check for content parity. KV cache and tokenization differences will be the trickiest part.
Leila - Solutions: Example mapping snippet we can offer to the customer (they asked for quick sample):
```
// shim pseudo
POST /rivalapi/chat -> /redwood/v1/chat
if (req.stop) mapStop(req.stop)
if (req.stream) enable_streaming()
onResponse(resp) {
  // rename fields to rival's names
  resp.message_text = resp.output
  resp.functions = resp.tools || []
}
```
Mia - Sales: Good. They also want to know pricing impact — if we add a shim and reindex embeddings, is there an obvious cost delta to show them for the POC?
Oliver (Eng): For the POC: reindexing embeddings is the biggest one-time cost (compute + storage). Runtime: streaming vs non-streaming doesn't materially change per-token cost, but if we need to keep dual models for fallback (smaller cheap model + full model) that impacts committed capacity. Estimate: one-off reindex job of a 100k-doc index on p4-ish infra ~ 8–12k USD, depending on quantization; runtime delta negligible unless they require reserved Dedicated capacity.
Raj - SecOps: On the security questionnaire front — they asked about: data residency, KMS/HSM support, SOC2, VPC/private deployment, audit logs retention, and egress controls. Short answers: SOC2: yes. KMS: integrates with customer KMS for Private. VPC: Private deployment available. Audit logs: configurable retention. Need to know if their legal team needs encrypted snapshots + physical data location.
salesbot: Link to internal pricing calc: https://redwood.internal/pricing-calc (run with customer index size, qps) :information_source:
secops-bot: Ran automated checklist for BlueHarbor (POC): policy-check OK, no public keys exposed, storage encryption: enabled — report at https://artifacts.redwood/blueharbor-poc-report.pdf
Sam W: Great. Can Eng produce a short eval script to show prompt parity diffs? We need to demo to their ML lead in 3 business days.
Oliver (Eng): Will do. Plan: create a small harness that replays 200 prompts through RivalAPI and Redwood shim, compute BLEU/ROUGE + token delta, and surface examples where the shim diverges. I can have a prototype by EOD tomorrow.
Leila - Solutions: I'll prepare a checklist for the migration POC: 1) Endpoint mapping doc (stop behavior, streaming semantics) 2) Field-name mapping examples 3) Reindex plan + cost estimate 4) Security questionnaire answers + contacts 5) Test harness + sample reports
Mia - Sales: Assign owners? Sam to own exec comms, Leila to own migration doc, Oliver to own harness, Raj to complete sec questionnaire. Can we aim for a 3-day POC plan and a 2-week migration playbook?
Raj - SecOps: I'll intake the questionnaire — send me their standard doc. If they require on-prem, we'll need Legal loop and timeline will expand.
Sam W: I'll send their questionnaire PDF now and schedule the demo with their ML lead for Thursday 1pm PT. @Leila @Oliver @Raj please confirm availability.
Leila - Solutions: Confirmed.
Oliver (Eng): Confirmed — will have prototype harness.
Raj - SecOps: Confirmed — I'll draft the security responses and flag anything that needs legal.
Mia - Sales: Perfect. I'll update the CRM and send BlueHarbor a short runbook with the next steps + cost sketch.
Sam W: Thanks team. Small ask: if we build the shim, should we offer it as an open-source sample or internal client-only script? Opinions?
Leila - Solutions: I vote open-source sample — helps other migrations and reduces engineering churn. Add a note: not production hardened.
Oliver (Eng): Fine with OSS sample as long as secrets and infra specifics are omitted.
Raj - SecOps: OSS ok for sample code; anything that touches config for Private deployments must stay internal.
Mia - Sales: Agreed. I'll include an OSS link and an enterprise integration appendix in the POC docs. :thumbsup:
Sam W: Great. Closing loop — demo scheduled, owners assigned. I'll post results after the run.
